core_obligations: Replace the first complex by a bounded complex of flat modules concentrated in the first interval (proof lines 17077-17081).
For an arbitrary module over the base ring, choose a free resolution and identify the triple derived tensor product with the total complex of a double complex (proof lines 17081-17089).
Use the hypothesis on the second complex to see that the inner total complex has cohomology only in the second interval (proof lines 17089-17092).
Apply the spectral sequence of the double complex to bound the cohomology of the tensor product by the sum of the intervals, which is the statement (proof lines 17092-17096).
proof_roadmap: Choose a resolution and identify the triple complex (proof lines 17081-17089).
Locate the cohomology of the inner complex (proof lines 17089-17092).
Apply the double complex spectral sequence (proof lines 17092-17097).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the tor amplitude of the derived tensor product of a complex over one ring with a complex over another ring as the sum of the two intervals, and the proof is a 21-line argument combining a reduction, a triple complex identity and a spectral sequence. It first replaces the first complex by a bounded complex of flat modules in the given interval, then for an arbitrary module over the base ring chooses a free resolution, identifies the triple tensor product with the total complex of a double complex whose second factor has cohomology concentrated in the second interval, and finally applies the spectral sequence of that double complex to bound the cohomology of the whole tensor product by the sum of the intervals. Each of the three ingredients is displayed.
